audit_findings.title: The DCF may double-count FY2026 cash generation
audit_findings.mechanism: The September 30, 2025 OE anchor may generate forecast cash flows already accumulated in the June 30, 2026 cash bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: References to Fiscal 2025, Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2023 used throughout this Annual Report relate to our fiscal years ended September 30, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The nine-month date mismatch is demonstrated, but actual double-counting cannot be established without the forecast schedule. The potential is material because the filed nine-month FY2026 net income was $139.437 million and operating cash flow was $195.038 million, although neither equals owner earnings or quantifies the overlap.
audit_findings.action: Show every forecast and discount date, then either roll the operating DCF forward to June 30, 2026 using a separately computed stub-period OE or use a September 30, 2025 balance-sheet bridge and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may include customer advances that are not excess cash
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash required to satisfy contract liabilities and associated project costs should remain in operating working capital rather than be added as excess cash in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Contract liabilities typically represent advance payments from contractual billing milestones and billings in excess of revenue recognized.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated dollar-for-dollar error, because cash is not earmarked to individual contract liabilities. It is reasonably capable of materially reducing value: at June 30, 2026, the filed net contract-liability position was $350.360 million against the $633.561 million cash bridge, and it had increased by $189.090 million since FY2025 while cash increased by $158.034 million.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile cash receipts, contract assets, contract liabilities and estimated remaining project costs contract by contract; establish normalized working-capital and liquidity requirements, then rerun the bridge using only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: The latest-actual anchor retains unusually favorable contract re-estimates
audit_findings.magnitude: $19.2 million pre-tax, equal to 12.0% of the $160.0 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Any nonrepeatable portion inflates anchor OE and therefore every forecast-period OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: For the years ended September 30, 2025 and 2024, our operating results were positively impacted by $ 19.2 million and $ 16.9 million, respectively, as a result of net changes in contract estimates related to projects in progress at the beginning of the respective period.
audit_findings.explanation: The $19.2 million FY2025 benefit is demonstrated, including $4.6 million from cancellations, but the record cannot establish how much is nonrepeatable. Similar favorable changes were $16.9 million in FY2024 and $12.8 million for the first nine months of FY2026, so removing the entire amount would also be unsupported. Materiality therefore remains uncertain.
audit_findings.action: Separate the $4.6 million cancellation benefit from execution, cost-estimate and variable-consideration revisions; assess each category across completed project cycles and rerun all scenarios with the supported normalized anchor.

audit_findings.title: At least $60 million of cash may be operationally unavailable
audit_findings.magnitude: $60.0 million, or $1.64 per diluted share and 2.1% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Required liquidity would reduce excess cash added through the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Additionally, we must maintain a consolidated cash balance of $ 60 million at all times, which can be deducted from the letters of credit outstanding as noted above.
audit_findings.explanation: The FY2025 filing establishes a $60 million minimum consolidated cash covenant, and the June 2026 filing reports compliance with the revolver covenants. Deducting $60 million would reduce base value from $78.72 to approximately $77.08 per share and the $55.10 buy-below level by approximately $1.15; neither approaches the $181.17 market price, so this amount cannot change the valuation conclusion. Additional collateral remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that the covenant remained unchanged at June 30, 2026, identify any separately required cash collateral, and rerun the bridge with the confirmed reserve.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration may be an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.428 million, or approximately $0.07 per diluted share and 0.08% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The remaining acquisition payment is a liability that should be deducted in the equity bridge if its principal settlement is not captured in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As of September 30, 2025, we determined the fair value of the contingent consideration was $ 2.3 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q demonstrates that the obligation remained outstanding at $2.428 million. Deducting it would reduce base value from $78.72 to approximately $78.65 per share, far too little to affect the conclusion relative to the $181.17 price.
audit_findings.action: Deduct the June 30, 2026 fair-value liability from the bridge, or document any post-quarter settlement or cancellation, and update the per-share value.

audit_findings.title: Foreign cash may carry a repatriation tax haircut
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the maximum filed foreign-cash exposure is $125.8 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Withholding or incremental U.S. taxes would reduce the realizable cash included in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: In the event that we elect to repatriate some or all of the foreign earnings that were previously deemed to be indefinitely reinvested outside the U.S., we may incur additional tax expense upon such repatriation under current tax laws.
audit_findings.explanation: The tax liability is an unresolved possibility because the filing says it is not practical to estimate and does not provide the foreign cash tax basis. Nevertheless, even writing off the entire $125.8 million foreign cash balance—an upper bound much larger than a tax haircut—would reduce base value by only $3.44 per share, from $78.72 to approximately $75.28, and would not change the conclusion relative to the $181.17 price.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the jurisdictional cash balances, tax bases, withholding rates and intended remittance paths; apply only the computed tax leakage to the bridge.
